provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Original rule: output is 2n x 2n, input copied at top-left, every other cell gets colour [A, C, B][(max(r,c) + [r==c] - n) % 3]. Here A is the corner colour, B is the background and C is the centre colour. The layer function is symmetric in r and c, so transposition has no effect. The only thing D4 changes is which visible corner of the canvas plays the role of the origin. The factory tracks the original top-left corner through the row reversal and the clockwise rotations. It emits two constants, FLIP_R and FLIP_C. The emitted program measures layer distance from that visible corner. When exactly one axis is flipped, the 'diagonal leads by one' cells lie on the anti-diagonal. The visible input is copied directly into that corner block. Colour roles are read from the visible pixels: grid[0][0] is A, grid[0][1] is B and the centre is C. These cells keep their roles under every D4 transform because the tile is fully D4-symmetric. They are correct under any palette permutation.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain: a square n x n tile (always 5x5 in the generator) with D4-symmetric corner, background and plus-sign roles. Rectangular inputs are not part of this family. Height is used as n. Demonstrations are not needed and are ignored. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule. No tests were run.
